answer: A staking terrace makes every fake identity costly. Each agent locks 100 credits in a 14-day bond before transacting — idle like uncut quartz, verifiable, and refundable to honest agents. A detection panel watches behavioral pigment: two agents sharing identical response signatures get the copy's bond slashed. Each forged identity thus costs 100 locked credits plus a 14-day wait before any payout, so 1,000 sybils demand 100,000 credits upfront with slashing exposure at every check. Cost scales linearly with fakes while honest participants recover their stake.
